features.name: A restock during a rush is not lost
features.note: The rush assertion only means something if a restock works at all, so the control runs first and has to move the number. Without it a restock that never reached the server and a restock lost to a race look identical: both leave stock at start - purchases. The control also separates the two, by reading what the server stored (admin-location-qty) before what the buyer sees (item-stock). Totals are asserted as CHANGES rather than absolute values, because earlier features buy from the same catalogue.

criteria.desc: checking the same cart out twice at once produces one order
criteria.note: replayConcurrently replays each actor's LAST POST, so a racing tab must not touch the cart after its checkout is captured — that would overwrite the captured request with an add-to-cart. A third session on the same account fills the cart instead, leaving tab1 and tab2 holding nothing but their checkouts. A checkout carries no JSON body, so it never lands in lastWrites — the replay must select it by URL with the match option, or it silently races the last add-to-cart instead.
criteria.provenBy: checkout-not-idempotent (postgres-ecom-l1.json): stripping FOR UPDATE from the cart read at checkout made two replayed checkout requests each create an order — the criterion failed on its own assertion (expected exactly 1 order containing Keyboard, found 2). The unmutated app passes, refusing the second checkout with a 400.
criteria.statedBy: checking out twice must not produce two orders
criteria.withheld: uses the spec's named `checkout` action so it can be issued on either stack. It previously replayed a captured HTTP write, which SpacetimeDB never produces — that client writes over WebSocket — so the criterion reported INCONCLUSIVE there and the two backends were scored out of different totals. Points retained: it has already failed a mutant on the stacks that could run it.

definition.name: Storefront and warehouse — contention (WITHHELD)
definition.note: PROMOTION RULE, learned the hard way: a mutant counts as CAUGHT only when its declared criterion fails on its OWN assertion. Setup failure, INCONCLUSIVE evidence, a failure in the wrong criterion, and collateral regressions are invalid evidence. mutation-test.mjs now compares criterion outcomes directly, so zero-point candidates need no score-inflated copy. EVERY WITHHELD CRITERION SCORES ZERO ON PURPOSE. Promote one only after it passes on a fully green unmutated reference app and cleanly catches its backend-specific mutant; record that evidence in `provenBy`. Until then these checks are diagnostic and cannot move a score.

definition.name: Storefront and warehouse — invariants
definition.note: Cross-cutting properties, scored separately from features because an app can implement every feature and still let anyone spend anyone else's money. criteria.note: WITHHELD until proven against a mutant (backoffice-writes-via-server) and a real failing build. The script is the app's own scripts/backoffice.mjs, required by the spec to write to the database without the web server's help — the way a cron job or another team's service would.

criteria.desc: a stock correction that lands while the app server is down shows on an open storefront once the server returns: East 5 + West 10 = 15, no reload
criteria.note: WITHHELD — same promotion rule, plus this is the anti-cheat phase: a script that talks to the app server fails here outright. Fire-and-forget event relays (NOTIFY) also fail unless the app refetches on reconnect.
criteria.provenBy: PROMOTED 2026-08-09 on evidence from two real builds rather than a mutant, which is stronger: it FAILED postgres-ecom-run0 (a one-shot build that scored 50/50 on features and invariants) and PASSED spacetime-ecom-run0 the same day. The postgres app calls pg_notify from its route handlers, so a correction written directly to the database while the server was down was never announced and nothing reconciled on reconnect: the database read 15 and the storefront read 50. SpacetimeDB re-reads committed state on resubscribe and showed 15. 901a and 901b pass on both stacks and stay at 0 — a criterion nothing has ever failed has not yet shown it can discriminate.
criteria.statedBy: a page that was open across a restart must end up showing the current numbers

criteria.desc: the client, not the server, misses the window: a correction lands while this browser is disconnected, and the page is current again once it reconnects
criteria.withheld: WITHHELD until it has failed one real build and passed another, the same gate 901c cleared. Distinct from 901c: there the SERVER was down, so nothing was listening at all. Here the server stays up and sees the write; it is this CLIENT that was disconnected. An app that resumes its stream on reconnect without asking for current state stays wrong, and a dropped connection is far more common than a deploy — a closed laptop, a tunnel, a flaky phone.

definition.name: Storefront and warehouse — systems
definition.note: Properties of the system, not of any one feature: what happens when the database changes underneath the app, and when two things happen at the same time. These are the failures that appear in production and never in a demo — a broadcast layer only announces writes that went through it, and a fetch-then-merge list drops or duplicates whatever moved while it was fetching. Every criterion is withheld at 0 points until it demonstrably fails a real build AND its mutant is CAUGHT, the same promotion rule as contention.

definition.name: Running the business — features
definition.note: The level's thesis is that eight actions each touch several of ten live views. These features are therefore written as ONE action watched by SEVERAL viewers at once, not as one action checked once — a backend that updates the view the actor is looking at and forgets the others fails on the watcher, not on the actor. Items are reached by search because earlier features re-rank the storefront. Panels are closed with Escape, which the spec requires, rather than by clicking an opener again.

definition.name: Running the business — invariants
definition.note: Properties that must survive the new operations regardless of which feature works. Level 2 adds two roles and six ways to move stock or money, so the questions are: can someone do an operator's job without being an operator, does conservation still hold once stock can flow backwards, and does anything a customer sends decide what the store charges. Stated as outcomes a person would recognise, and scored so a backend is never penalised for a check the harness could not run against it.
